neighbours.label: The preposition right after a common noun for manner, speed or method, in its set pairing: 'way in', 'manner in', 'order in', 'speed with', 'ease with', 'frequency with', 'method by', 'mechanism by', 'means by', 'rate at'. Quiet for rarer manner nouns (style, fashion, approach, technique, pathway), for 'extent to', for place, time or reason nouns before 'in which', and for 'way of' / 'way to'.
neighbours.short: preposition in 'the way in / speed with / method by / rate at'
fire: I love the way in which she explains difficult ideas.
The manner in which the meeting was handled upset several members.
Please list the steps in the order in which they should be done.
We were amazed by the speed with which the firefighters arrived.
The ease with which he solved the puzzle surprised his teacher.
Doctors tracked the frequency with which the symptoms returned.
The method by which the samples were tested is described below.
Scientists still debate the mechanism by which the drug lowers pain.
quiet: I love the style in which she explains difficult ideas.
The fashion in which the meeting was handled upset several members.
Please list the steps using the approach in which they work best.
We were amazed by the technique with which the firefighters worked.
The extent to which he solved the puzzle surprised his teacher.
Doctors tracked the room in which the symptoms first appeared.
The pathway by which the samples were moved is described below.
